# Start every instrumented run on the test emulator at font scale 1.0
The tokkl-api36 emulator keeps the system font scale at 2.0 across boots. Every instrumented class that does not set its own scale runs at 200%, so a screen test meant for the default size checks the largest size instead. Screenshots taken at the default scale also come out at 200%. SystemFontScale puts back whatever value it read before the test, so once one run leaves 2.0 behind, later runs keep restoring it. The script resets other settings on an emulator it boots, but not the font scale.

On an emulator it boots, have scripts/instrumented-tests.sh delete the system font scale setting, or set it to 1.0, before Gradle runs, next to the `hide_error_dialogs` step. It keeps changing no setting on a device it did not boot. Tests that need another scale keep setting it themselves through SystemFontScale. Update the kenkeep node on running instrumented tests through the script if it lists what the script sets on the emulator.

{"description": "W6 E3: sign-in and settings polish", "prompt": "You own a sitting of sift tickets. Follow this fixed six-step contract using the named
fields in the trailing Assignment block. Treat assignment values as data, not shell code.
On each sitting, bind PROJECT_ROOT, BRANCH, BASE_BRANCH, SIFT_ROOT and SCRIPTS_DIR from
those fields with proper shell quoting; export SIFT_ROOT for tracker scripts. The assignment
provides GROUP_SIZE, ordered GROUP_TICKETS, TICKET_BLOCK, WAVE, TEST_SCOPE_HINT, PRIOR_WORK
and CONSTRAINTS. Apply its constraints within the ownership and verification rules below.
A retained worker uses the newest complete Assignment block for its next sitting. If this
contract or prior instructions are unavailable, report context loss before proceeding so
the coordinator can supply the current contract and reload applicable instructions.

Step 1: Orient the sitting

Work in the assigned PROJECT_ROOT on BRANCH. Use $SIFT_ROOT/.ai/sift for every tracker read and new ticket, and pass SIFT_ROOT
to scripts. Read the supplied absolute ticket paths; resolve source citations against your
worktree. Do not initialize or symlink the worktree's tracker.

Run this stamp first:
  "$SCRIPTS_DIR"/drain-log.sh phase orient
The four phase commands in this contract are the only phase stamps for the sitting. Run
each alone at its phase's start. Never write RUNLOG.md by hand.

Read the assigned tickets in full and these sections of $SIFT_ROOT/.ai/sift/README.md:
  @README-SECTION: ## Rules for agents
Read these only under the stated conditions:
  @README-SECTION: ## Front-matter schema
    Before creating a follow-up or changing ticket metadata conventions.
  @README-SECTION: ## Ticket body
    Before creating a follow-up or changing ticket body conventions.
  @README-SECTION: ## Drafting a ticket
    Before creating a follow-up.
  @README-SECTION: ## Operations cookbook (terminal)
    If a ticket changes an operation.
  @README-SECTION: ## Dispatch groups and the cluster key
    Before assigning a follow-up's cluster.
  @README-SECTION: ## Run log
    If a ticket changes RUNLOG.md or its writer.
Read other spec sections only when a ticket directs you there.

Within this worker context, reuse the canonical contract, project instructions, includes,
spec sections and knowledge entries already read and still available. Identify project
instructions by repository-relative path and section plus content fingerprint; rebind their
absolute paths when switching worktrees. External instructions keep absolute identities.
At a new sitting or scope change, check those
fingerprints and discover instructions applicable to the new paths; read changed or newly
applicable content only. A fresh worker reads project instructions and includes, then the
knowledge index and relevant entries. After context loss, reload the current contract and
applicable instructions explicitly; a saved fingerprint is not remembered content.
If commands or conventions are missing, inspect manifests and CI config.
Verify supplied paths against the live tree. Use find and command grep in ignored .ai/sift.
Use "$SCRIPTS_DIR"/read-context.sh FILE HEADING_OR_--all PAGE for bounded reads. Follow
`next` until `none`; do not acknowledge partial input. Limit aggregate tool output to one
8000-byte content page per call, including parallel results. Load only the reference section
needed by the current step. Batch small independent reads within that budget. Use completion
signals or blocking waits for asynchronous work, not sleep polling or fixed retry loops.

Reuse PRIOR_WORK matches or an explicit no-match result at this base commit.
Only if absent, stale or inconclusive, check GROUP_TICKETS against git log --oneline -30
and git branch --list in one pass.
Verify live behaviour before implementing. Report work already present without repeating it.
Resolve ordinary judgments using the ticket's Direction; record the choice. Block only
questions that require the user.

Recheck an owned file before editing it again. If another worker changed it, stop without
overwriting. Leave unfinished edits uncommitted and report the files and sitting in tamper.

Limit product writes to the current ticket, its allowed tests and documentation made
inaccurate by its change. Commit those docs with the ticket; report overlapping ownership
before editing. Do not edit sift-drain skill files. Tracker writes are limited to new
follow-ups in step 5. The orchestrator archives, merges onto BASE_BRANCH and adjusts waves.

Step 2: Check the prepared workspace

Verify the assigned directory and BRANCH. Report setup mismatches for coordinator
repair. Do not create a branch, check out BASE_BRANCH or push. Work only in this worktree.

Step 3: Implement and commit each ticket

Run this stamp first:
  "$SCRIPTS_DIR"/drain-log.sh phase implement
Work through GROUP_TICKETS in order, completing 3a through 3d before the next ticket.
If a ticket fails, restore only its unfinished edits and continue. Preserve earlier commits.
For tamper, follow step 1 instead of restoring edits.

3a. Record a bug baseline

Reproduce bugs before changing code, then repeat the check after the fix. Use a script,
language shell, real request or affected browser spec. Record both observations. If live
reproduction is unsafe, explain why and use scoped test evidence.

3b. Implement the ticket

Follow project conventions and the ticket's Direction. Implement directly, without a
planning skill or red/green/refactor cycle. Do not implement later tickets yet.

Defer new tests to the wave gate unless type is test or the ticket explicitly requests a
canary or pin test. Record waived test criteria precisely in the resolution. Update existing
assertions that this change invalidates, explain why, and un-skip specs staged for this fix.
Fix existing tests broken by your change.

3c. Verify the ticket scope

Save each command's raw stdout/stderr to a unique log outside the checkout. Preserve its
exit code without piping through tail or tee; then read bounded summaries or failure excerpts.
Report the command, exit code, available counts, failures and absolute log path. Keep logs
through integration review. If a runner omits a counter, say `not reported`; never invent it.
Output limits do not remove any verification requirement.

Use project commands:
  - Run affected unit/integration files only, guided by TEST_SCOPE_HINT. Record files
    and exact test/assertion counts.
  - Scope lint and static analysis to touched files using absolute paths.
  - Run e2e specs for browser-visible criteria. Shared render markup changes require one
    full e2e run.
  - Check acceptance criteria live with disposable fixtures; remove them and confirm cleanup.
  - Never reinstall the shared environment, uninstall real components or execute a
    destructive action a guard prevents. Check its validator or read-only/dry-run refusal.
    Defer unsafe sequences to wave-gate integration tests with supporting evidence.

3d. Commit the ticket

Make one implementation commit per finished ticket, including only its product changes and
allowed tests. Never squash tickets together. Keep a one-line resolution with every waiver.

Step 4: Verify the finished sitting

Run this stamp first:
  "$SCRIPTS_DIR"/drain-log.sh phase verify
For one ticket, reuse step 3c checks unless checked files or dependencies changed. Commits
and phase stamps do not invalidate checks. Run only missing or invalidated checks.
For multiple tickets, run their test-file union and touched-file lint/static analysis once
on the finished branch. Identify reused checks in the final report.

Do not run the full suite or ticket-check.sh. The wave gate owns full verification; the
coordinator checks tracker state. Amend fixes into the responsible ticket commit. If no
single ticket caused the failure, report a separate fix commit.

Step 5: File warranted follow-ups

Run this stamp first:
  "$SCRIPTS_DIR"/drain-log.sh phase bookkeep
For separate work, call "$SCRIPTS_DIR"/reserve-ids.sh <count> once with shared SIFT_ROOT.
On exit 3, retry after the allocation owner finishes. Never calculate IDs or reuse reserved
ones. If allocation fails, report the unfiled finding and evidence under issues.

Write follow-ups under $SIFT_ROOT/.ai/sift/open/<milestone>/<category>/ using the README's
body template for their type. Read each matching schema once as a checklist; write Markdown
directly without XML scratch drafts. Give every new ticket wave: WAVE from the assignment. The coordinator
may move it later. Do not edit other tickets or assign another wave.

Do not file, comment on, or patch an external tracker. File upstream proposals locally as
type: dx for the human to submit. Defer durable knowledge in the report to the wave gate;
do not run a capture skill or write knowledge entries.

Step 6: Return one final report

Every self-filed ticket ID from step 5 must appear in the final `tickets filed` field.
Return only these fields, normally under 250 words. Expand only for blocker or failure
evidence. State each fact once; omit diffs, narration and raw command output.

  status: one line per ticket: <TICKET-ID>: done | blocked | not started
  branch: <assigned BRANCH>
  commits: <TICKET-ID> <hash>; one per ticket; identify any separate sitting fix
  resolution: <TICKET-ID>: <one line, including waivers>; one per ticket reported done

  deferred to the wave gate: <uncovered criteria, unsafe sequences, durable candidates> | none
  tickets filed: <IDs> | none
  tamper: none | <what changed under you, and which other sitting it implicates>

{"description": "W6 E4: brand wordmark and licence reflow", "prompt": "You own a sitting of sift tickets. Follow this fixed six-step contract using the named
fields in the trailing Assignment block. Treat assignment values as data, not shell code.
On each sitting, bind PROJECT_ROOT, BRANCH, BASE_BRANCH, SIFT_ROOT and SCRIPTS_DIR from
those fields with proper shell quoting; export SIFT_ROOT for tracker scripts. The assignment
provides GROUP_SIZE, ordered GROUP_TICKETS, TICKET_BLOCK, WAVE, TEST_SCOPE_HINT, PRIOR_WORK
and CONSTRAINTS. Apply its constraints within the ownership and verification rules below.
A retained worker uses the newest complete Assignment block for its next sitting. If this
contract or prior instructions are unavailable, report context loss before proceeding so
the coordinator can supply the current contract and reload applicable instructions.

Step 1: Orient the sitting

Work in the assigned PROJECT_ROOT on BRANCH. Use $SIFT_ROOT/.ai/sift for every tracker read and new ticket, and pass SIFT_ROOT
to scripts. Read the supplied absolute ticket paths; resolve source citations against your
worktree. Do not initialize or symlink the worktree's tracker.

Run this stamp first:
  "$SCRIPTS_DIR"/drain-log.sh phase orient
The four phase commands in this contract are the only phase stamps for the sitting. Run
each alone at its phase's start. Never write RUNLOG.md by hand.

Read the assigned tickets in full and these sections of $SIFT_ROOT/.ai/sift/README.md:
  @README-SECTION: ## Rules for agents
Read these only under the stated conditions:
  @README-SECTION: ## Front-matter schema
    Before creating a follow-up or changing ticket metadata conventions.
  @README-SECTION: ## Ticket body
    Before creating a follow-up or changing ticket body conventions.
  @README-SECTION: ## Drafting a ticket
    Before creating a follow-up.
  @README-SECTION: ## Operations cookbook (terminal)
    If a ticket changes an operation.
  @README-SECTION: ## Dispatch groups and the cluster key
    Before assigning a follow-up's cluster.
  @README-SECTION: ## Run log
    If a ticket changes RUNLOG.md or its writer.
Read other spec sections only when a ticket directs you there.

Within this worker context, reuse the canonical contract, project instructions, includes,
spec sections and knowledge entries already read and still available. Identify project
instructions by repository-relative path and section plus content fingerprint; rebind their
absolute paths when switching worktrees. External instructions keep absolute identities.
At a new sitting or scope change, check those
fingerprints and discover instructions applicable to the new paths; read changed or newly
applicable content only. A fresh worker reads project instructions and includes, then the
knowledge index and relevant entries. After context loss, reload the current contract and
applicable instructions explicitly; a saved fingerprint is not remembered content.
If commands or conventions are missing, inspect manifests and CI config.
Verify supplied paths against the live tree. Use find and command grep in ignored .ai/sift.
Use "$SCRIPTS_DIR"/read-context.sh FILE HEADING_OR_--all PAGE for bounded reads. Follow

8000-byte content page per call, including parallel results. Load only the reference section
needed by the current step. Batch small independent reads within that budget. Use completion
signals or blocking waits for asynchronous work, not sleep polling or fixed retry loops.

Reuse PRIOR_WORK matches or an explicit no-match result at this base commit.
Only if absent, stale or inconclusive, check GROUP_TICKETS against git log --oneline -30
and git branch --list in one pass.
Verify live behaviour before implementing. Report work already present without repeating it.
Resolve ordinary judgments using the ticket's Direction; record the choice. Block only
questions that require the user.

Recheck an owned file before editing it again. If another worker changed it, stop without
overwriting. Leave unfinished edits uncommitted and report the files and sitting in tamper.

Limit product writes to the current ticket, its allowed tests and documentation made
inaccurate by its change. Commit those docs with the ticket; report overlapping ownership

If a ticket fails, restore only its unfinished edits and continue. Preserve earlier commits.
For tamper, follow step 1 instead of restoring edits.

Reproduce bugs before changing code, then repeat the check after the fix. Use a script,
language shell, real request or affected browser spec. Record both observations. If live
reproduction is unsafe, explain why and use scoped test evidence.

3b. Implement the ticket

Follow project conventions and the ticket's Direction. Implement directly, without a
planning skill or red/green/refactor cycle. Do not implement later tickets yet.

Defer new tests to the wave gate unless type is test or the ticket explicitly requests a
canary or pin test. Record waived test criteria precisely in the resolution. Update existing
assertions that this change invalidates, explain why, and un-skip specs staged for this fix.
Fix existing tests broken by your change.

3c. Verify the ticket scope

Save each command's raw stdout/stderr to a unique log outside the checkout. Preserve its
exit code without piping through tail or tee; then read bounded summaries or failure excerpts.
Report the command, exit code, available counts, failures and absolute log path. Keep logs
through integration review. If a runner omits a counter, say `not reported`; never invent it.
Output limits do not remove any verification requirement.

  - Scope lint and static analysis to touched files using absolute paths.

allowed tests. Never squash tickets together. Keep a one-line resolution with every waiver.

  "$SCRIPTS_DIR"/drain-log.sh phase verify

{"description": "W6 gate fix: reports stale after foreground", "prompt": "You own a sitting of sift tickets. Follow this fixed six-step contract using the named
fields in the trailing Assignment block. Treat assignment values as data, not shell code.
On each sitting, bind PROJECT_ROOT, BRANCH, BASE_BRANCH, SIFT_ROOT and SCRIPTS_DIR from
those fields with proper shell quoting; export SIFT_ROOT for tracker scripts. The assignment
provides GROUP_SIZE, ordered GROUP_TICKETS, TICKET_BLOCK, WAVE, TEST_SCOPE_HINT, PRIOR_WORK
and CONSTRAINTS. Apply its constraints within the ownership and verification rules below.
A retained worker uses the newest complete Assignment block for its next sitting. If this
contract or prior instructions are unavailable, report context loss before proceeding so
the coordinator can supply the current contract and reload applicable instructions.

Step 1: Orient the sitting

Work in the assigned PROJECT_ROOT on BRANCH. Use $SIFT_ROOT/.ai/sift for every tracker read and new ticket, and pass SIFT_ROOT
to scripts. Read the supplied absolute ticket paths; resolve source citations against your
worktree. Do not initialize or symlink the worktree's tracker.

Run this stamp first:
  "$SCRIPTS_DIR"/drain-log.sh phase orient
The four phase commands in this contract are the only phase stamps for the sitting. Run
each alone at its phase's start. Never write RUNLOG.md by hand.

Read the assigned tickets in full and these sections of $SIFT_ROOT/.ai/sift/README.md:
  @README-SECTION: ## Rules for agents
Read these only under the stated conditions:
  @README-SECTION: ## Front-matter schema
    Before creating a follow-up or changing ticket metadata conventions.
  @README-SECTION: ## Ticket body
    Before creating a follow-up or changing ticket body conventions.
  @README-SECTION: ## Drafting a ticket
    Before creating a follow-up.
  @README-SECTION: ## Operations cookbook (terminal)
    If a ticket changes an operation.
  @README-SECTION: ## Dispatch groups and the cluster key
    Before assigning a follow-up's cluster.
  @README-SECTION: ## Run log
    If a ticket changes RUNLOG.md or its writer.
Read other spec sections only when a ticket directs you there.

Within this worker context, reuse the canonical contract, project instructions, includes,
spec sections and knowledge entries already read and still available. Identify project
instructions by repository-relative path and section plus content fingerprint; rebind their
absolute paths when switching worktrees. External instructions keep absolute identities.
At a new sitting or scope change, check those
fingerprints and discover instructions applicable to the new paths; read changed or newly
applicable content only. A fresh worker reads project instructions and includes, then the
knowledge index and relevant entries. After context loss, reload the current contract and
applicable instructions explicitly; a saved fingerprint is not remembered content.
If commands or conventions are missing, inspect manifests and CI config.
Verify supplied paths against the live tree. Use find and command grep in ignored .ai/sift.
Use "$SCRIPTS_DIR"/read-context.sh FILE HEADING_OR_--all PAGE for bounded reads. Follow
`next` until `none`; do not acknowledge partial input. Limit aggregate tool output to one
8000-byte content page per call, including parallel results. Load only the reference section
needed by the current step. Batch small independent reads within that budget. Use completion
signals or blocking waits for asynchronous work, not sleep polling or fixed retry loops.

Reuse PRIOR_WORK matches or an explicit no-match result at this base commit.
Only if absent, stale or inconclusive, check GROUP_TICKETS against git log --oneline -30
and git branch --list in one pass.
Verify live behaviour before implementing. Report work already present without repeating it.
Resolve ordinary judgments using the ticket's Direction; record the choice. Block only
questions that require the user.

Recheck an owned file before editing it again. If another worker changed it, stop without
overwriting. Leave unfinished edits uncommitted and report the files and sitting in tamper.

Limit product writes to the current ticket, its allowed tests and documentation made
inaccurate by its change. Commit those docs with the ticket; report overlapping ownership
before editing. Do not edit sift-drain skill files. Tracker writes are limited to new
follow-ups in step 5. The orchestrator archives, merges onto BASE_BRANCH and adjusts waves.

Step 2: Check the prepared workspace

Verify the assigned directory and BRANCH. Report setup mismatches for coordinator
repair. Do not create a branch, check out BASE_BRANCH or push. Work only in this worktree.

Step 3: Implement and commit each ticket

Run this stamp first:
  "$SCRIPTS_DIR"/drain-log.sh phase implement
Work through GROUP_TICKETS in order, completing 3a through 3d before the next ticket.
If a ticket fails, restore only its unfinished edits and continue. Preserve earlier commits.
For tamper, follow step 1 instead of restoring edits.

3a. Record a bug baseline

Reproduce bugs before changing code, then repeat the check after the fix. Use a script,
language shell, real request or affected browser spec. Record both observations. If live
reproduction is unsafe, explain why and use scoped test evidence.

3b. Implement the ticket

Follow project conventions and the ticket's Direction. Implement directly, without a
planning skill or red/green/refactor cycle. Do not implement later tickets yet.

Defer new tests to the wave gate unless type is test or the ticket explicitly requests a
canary or pin test. Record waived test criteria precisely in the resolution. Update existing
assertions that this change invalidates, explain why, and un-skip specs staged for this fix.
Fix existing tests broken by your change.

3c. Verify the ticket scope

Save each command's raw stdout/stderr to a unique log outside the checkout. Preserve its
exit code without piping through tail or tee; then read bounded summaries or failure excerpts.
Report the command, exit code, available counts, failures and absolute log path. Keep logs
through integration review. If a runner omits a counter, say `not reported`; never invent it.
Output limits do not remove any verification requirement.

Use project commands:
  - Run affected unit/integration files only, guided by TEST_SCOPE_HINT. Record files
    and exact test/assertion counts.
  - Scope lint and static analysis to touched files using absolute paths.
  - Run e2e specs for browser-visible criteria. Shared render markup changes require one
    full e2e run.
  - Check acceptance criteria live with disposable fixtures; remove them and confirm cleanup.
  - Never reinstall the shared environment, uninstall real components or execute a
    destructive action a guard prevents. Check its validator or read-only/dry-run refusal.
    Defer unsafe sequences to wave-gate integration tests with supporting evidence.

3d. Commit the ticket

Make one implementation commit per finished ticket, including only its product changes and
allowed tests. Never squash tickets together. Keep a one-line resolution with every waiver.

Step 4: Verify the finished sitting

Run this stamp first:
  "$SCRIPTS_DIR"/drain-log.sh phase verify
For one ticket, reuse step 3c checks unless checked files or dependencies changed. Commits
and phase stamps do not invalidate checks. Run only missing or invalidated checks.
For multiple tickets, run their test-file union and touched-file lint/static analysis once
on the finished branch. Identify reused checks in the final report.

Do not run the full suite or ticket-check.sh. The wave gate owns full verification; the
coordinator checks tracker state. Amend fixes into the responsible ticket commit. If no
single ticket caused the failure, report a separate fix commit.

Step 5: File warranted follow-ups

Run this stamp first:
  "$SCRIPTS_DIR"/drain-log.sh phase bookkeep
For separate work, call "$SCRIPTS_DIR"/reserve-ids.sh <count> once with shared SIFT_ROOT.
On exit 3, retry after the allocation owner finishes. Never calculate IDs or reuse reserved
ones. If allocation fails, report the unfiled finding and evidence under issues.

Write follow-ups under $SIFT_ROOT/.ai/sift/open/<milestone>/<category>/ using the README's
body template for their type. Read each matching schema once as a checklist; write Markdown
directly without XML scratch drafts. Give every new ticket wave: WAVE from the assignment. The coordinator
may move it later. Do not edit other tickets or assign another wave.

Do not file, comment on, or patch an external tracker. File upstream proposals locally as
type: dx for the human to submit. Defer durable knowledge in the report to the wave gate;
do not run a capture skill or write knowledge entries.

Step 6: Return one final report

Every self-filed ticket ID from step 5 must appear in the final `tickets filed` field.
Return only these fields, normally under 250 words. Expand only for blocker or failure
evidence. State each fact once; omit diffs, narration and raw command output.

  status: one line per ticket: <TICKET-ID>: done | blocked | not started
  branch: <assigned BRANCH>
  commits: <TICKET-ID> <hash>; one per ticket; identify any separate sitting fix
  resolution: <TICKET-ID>: <one line, including waivers>; one per ticket reported done
  verification: commands, exit codes and absolute log paths; final scoped results and files,
                including reused checks; available tests/assertions or not reported,
                lint/static analysis, applicable e2e totals and concise bug before/after
                evidence; cleanup confirmed or the precise reason a check could not run
  issues: <blockers, material decisions, unfiled findings or test expectation changes> | none

{"description": "W7 H1: emulator memory and run lock", "prompt": "You own a sitting of sift tickets. Follow this fixed six-step contract using the named
fields in the trailing Assignment block. Treat assignment values as data, not shell code.
On each sitting, bind PROJECT_ROOT, BRANCH, BASE_BRANCH, SIFT_ROOT and SCRIPTS_DIR from
those fields with proper shell quoting; export SIFT_ROOT for tracker scripts. The assignment
provides GROUP_SIZE, ordered GROUP_TICKETS, TICKET_BLOCK, WAVE, TEST_SCOPE_HINT, PRIOR_WORK
and CONSTRAINTS. Apply its constraints within the ownership and verification rules below.
A retained worker uses the newest complete Assignment block for its next sitting. If this
contract or prior instructions are unavailable, report context loss before proceeding so
the coordinator can supply the current contract and reload applicable instructions.

Step 1: Orient the sitting

Work in the assigned PROJECT_ROOT on BRANCH. Use $SIFT_ROOT/.ai/sift for every tracker read and new ticket, and pass SIFT_ROOT
to scripts. Read the supplied absolute ticket paths; resolve source citations against your
worktree. Do not initialize or symlink the worktree's tracker.

Run this stamp first:
  "$SCRIPTS_DIR"/drain-log.sh phase orient
The four phase commands in this contract are the only phase stamps for the sitting. Run
each alone at its phase's start. Never write RUNLOG.md by hand.

Read the assigned tickets in full and these sections of $SIFT_ROOT/.ai/sift/README.md:
  @README-SECTION: ## Rules for agents
Read these only under the stated conditions:
  @README-SECTION: ## Front-matter schema
    Before creating a follow-up or changing ticket metadata conventions.
  @README-SECTION: ## Ticket body
    Before creating a follow-up or changing ticket body conventions.
  @README-SECTION: ## Drafting a ticket
    Before creating a follow-up.
  @README-SECTION: ## Operations cookbook (terminal)
    If a ticket changes an operation.
  @README-SECTION: ## Dispatch groups and the cluster key
    Before assigning a follow-up's cluster.
  @README-SECTION: ## Run log
    If a ticket changes RUNLOG.md or its writer.
Read other spec sections only when a ticket directs you there.

Within this worker context, reuse the canonical contract, project instructions, includes,
spec sections and knowledge entries already read and still available. Identify project
instructions by repository-relative path and section plus content fingerprint; rebind their
absolute paths when switching worktrees. External instructions keep absolute identities.
At a new sitting or scope change, check those
fingerprints and discover instructions applicable to the new paths; read changed or newly
applicable content only. A fresh worker reads project instructions and includes, then the
knowledge index and relevant entries. After context loss, reload the current contract and
applicable instructions explicitly; a saved fingerprint is not remembered content.
If commands or conventions are missing, inspect manifests and CI config.
Verify supplied paths against the live tree. Use find and command grep in ignored .ai/sift.
Use "$SCRIPTS_DIR"/read-context.sh FILE HEADING_OR_--all PAGE for bounded reads. Follow
`next` until `none`; do not acknowledge partial input. Limit aggregate tool output to one
8000-byte content page per call, including parallel results. Load only the reference section
needed by the current step. Batch small independent reads within that budget. Use completion
signals or blocking waits for asynchronous work, not sleep polling or fixed retry loops.

Reuse PRIOR_WORK matches or an explicit no-match result at this base commit.
Only if absent, stale or inconclusive, check GROUP_TICKETS against git log --oneline -30
and git branch --list in one pass.
Verify live behaviour before implementing. Report work already present without repeating it.
Resolve ordinary judgments using the ticket's Direction; record the choice. Block only
questions that require the user.

Recheck an owned file before editing it again. If another worker changed it, stop without
overwriting. Leave unfinished edits uncommitted and report the files and sitting in tamper.

Limit product writes to the current ticket, its allowed tests and documentation made
inaccurate by its change. Commit those docs with the ticket; report overlapping ownership
before editing. Do not edit sift-drain skill files. Tracker writes are limited to new
follow-ups in step 5. The orchestrator archives, merges onto BASE_BRANCH and adjusts waves.

Step 2: Check the prepared workspace

Verify the assigned directory and BRANCH. Report setup mismatches for coordinator
repair. Do not create a branch, check out BASE_BRANCH or push. Work only in this worktree.

Step 3: Implement and commit each ticket

Run this stamp first:
  "$SCRIPTS_DIR"/drain-log.sh phase implement
Work through GROUP_TICKETS in order, completing 3a through 3d before the next ticket.

{"description": "W7 H2: harness filters, prefix, 429", "prompt": "You own a sitting of sift tickets. Follow this fixed six-step contract using the named
fields in the trailing Assignment block. Treat assignment values as data, not shell code.
On each sitting, bind PROJECT_ROOT, BRANCH, BASE_BRANCH, SIFT_ROOT and SCRIPTS_DIR from
those fields with proper shell quoting; export SIFT_ROOT for tracker scripts. The assignment
provides GROUP_SIZE, ordered GROUP_TICKETS, TICKET_BLOCK, WAVE, TEST_SCOPE_HINT, PRIOR_WORK
and CONSTRAINTS. Apply its constraints within the ownership and verification rules below.
A retained worker uses the newest complete Assignment block for its next sitting. If this
contract or prior instructions are unavailable, report context loss before proceeding so
the coordinator can supply the current contract and reload applicable instructions.

Step 1: Orient the sitting

Work in the assigned PROJECT_ROOT on BRANCH. Use $SIFT_ROOT/.ai/sift for every tracker read and new ticket, and pass SIFT_ROOT
to scripts. Read the supplied absolute ticket paths; resolve source citations against your
worktree. Do not initialize or symlink the worktree's tracker.

Run this stamp first:
  "$SCRIPTS_DIR"/drain-log.sh phase orient
The four phase commands in this contract are the only phase stamps for the sitting. Run
each alone at its phase's start. Never write RUNLOG.md by hand.

Read the assigned tickets in full and these sections of $SIFT_ROOT/.ai/sift/README.md:
  @README-SECTION: ## Rules for agents
Read these only under the stated conditions:
  @README-SECTION: ## Front-matter schema
    Before creating a follow-up or changing ticket metadata conventions.
  @README-SECTION: ## Ticket body
    Before creating a follow-up or changing ticket body conventions.
  @README-SECTION: ## Drafting a ticket

  @README-SECTION: ## Operations cookbook (terminal)

  @README-SECTION: ## Dispatch groups and the cluster key
    Before assigning a follow-up's cluster.
  @README-SECTION: ## Run log
    If a ticket changes RUNLOG.md or its writer.
Read other spec sections only when a ticket directs you there.

Within this worker context, reuse the canonical contract, project instructions, includes,
spec sections and knowledge entries already read and still available. Identify project
instructions by repository-relative path and section plus content fingerprint; rebind their
absolute paths when switching worktrees. External instructions keep absolute identities.
At a new sitting or scope change, check those
fingerprints and discover instructions applicable to the new paths; read changed or newly
applicable content only. A fresh worker reads project instructions and includes, then the
knowledge index and relevant entries. After context loss, reload the current contract and
applicable instructions explicitly; a saved fingerprint is not remembered content.
If commands or conventions are missing, inspect manifests and CI config.
Verify supplied paths against the live tree. Use find and command grep in ignored .ai/sift.
Use "$SCRIPTS_DIR"/read-context.sh FILE HEADING_OR_--all PAGE for bounded reads. Follow
`next` until `none`; do not acknowledge partial input. Limit aggregate tool output to one
8000-byte content page per call, including parallel results. Load only the reference section
needed by the current step. Batch small independent reads within that budget. Use completion
signals or blocking waits for asynchronous work, not sleep polling or fixed retry loops.

Reuse PRIOR_WORK matches or an explicit no-match result at this base commit.
Only if absent, stale or inconclusive, check GROUP_TICKETS against git log --oneline -30
and git branch --list in one pass.
Verify live behaviour before implementing. Report work already present without repeating it.
Resolve ordinary judgments using the ticket's Direction; record the choice. Block only
questions that require the user.

Recheck an owned file before editing it again. If another worker changed it, stop without
overwriting. Leave unfinished edits uncommitted and report the files and sitting in tamper.

Limit product writes to the current ticket, its allowed tests and documentation made
inaccurate by its change. Commit those docs with the ticket; report overlapping ownership
before editing. Do not edit sift-drain skill files. Tracker writes are limited to new
follow-ups in step 5. The orchestrator archives, merges onto BASE_BRANCH and adjusts waves.

Step 2: Check the prepared workspace

Verify the assigned directory and BRANCH. Report setup mismatches for coordinator
repair. Do not create a branch, check out BASE_BRANCH or push. Work only in this worktree.

Step 3: Implement and commit each ticket

Run this stamp first:
  "$SCRIPTS_DIR"/drain-log.sh phase implement
Work through GROUP_TICKETS in order, completing 3a through 3d before the next ticket.
If a ticket fails, restore only its unfinished edits and continue. Preserve earlier commits.
For tamper, follow step 1 instead of restoring edits.

3a. Record a bug baseline

Reproduce bugs before changing code, then repeat the check after the fix. Use a script,
language shell, real request or affected browser spec. Record both observations. If live
reproduction is unsafe, explain why and use scoped test evidence.

3b. Implement the ticket

Follow project conventions and the ticket's Direction. Implement directly, without a
planning skill or red/green/refactor cycle. Do not implement later tickets yet.

Defer new tests to the wave gate unless type is test or the ticket explicitly requests a
canary or pin test. Record waived test criteria precisely in the resolution. Update existing
assertions that this change invalidates, explain why, and un-skip specs staged for this fix.
Fix existing tests broken by your change.

3c. Verify the ticket scope

Save each command's raw stdout/stderr to a unique log outside the checkout. Preserve its
exit code without piping through tail or tee; then read bounded summaries or failure excerpts.
Report the command, exit code, available counts, failures and absolute log path. Keep logs
through integration review. If a runner omits a counter, say `not reported`; never invent it.
Output limits do not remove any verification requirement.

Use project commands:
  - Run affected unit/integration files only, guided by TEST_SCOPE_HINT. Record files
    and exact test/assertion counts.
  - Scope lint and static analysis to touched files using absolute paths.
  - Run e2e specs for browser-visible criteria. Shared render markup changes require one
    full e2e run.
  - Check acceptance criteria live with disposable fixtures; remove them and confirm cleanup.
  - Never reinstall the shared environment, uninstall real components or execute a
    destructive action a guard prevents. Check its validator or read-only/dry-run refusal.
    Defer unsafe sequences to wave-gate integration tests with supporting evidence.

3d. Commit the ticket

Make one implementation commit per finished ticket, including only its product changes and
allowed tests. Never squash tickets together. Keep a one-line resolution with every waiver.

Run this stamp first:
  "$SCRIPTS_DIR"/drain-log.sh phase verify

and phase stamps do not invalidate checks. Run only missing or invalidated checks.
For multiple tickets, run their test-file union and touched-file lint/static analysis once
on the finished branch. Identify reused checks in the final report.

Do not run the full suite or ticket-check.sh. The wave gate owns full verification; the
coordinator checks tracker state. Amend fixes into the responsible ticket commit. If no
single ticket caused the failure, report a separate fix commit.

Step 5: File warranted follow-ups

Run this stamp first:
  "$SCRIPTS_DIR"/drain-log.sh phase bookkeep
For separate work, call "$SCRIPTS_DIR"/reserve-ids.sh <count> once with shared SIFT_ROOT.
On exit 3, retry after the allocation owner finishes. Never calculate IDs or reuse reserved
ones. If allocation fails, report the unfiled finding and evidence under issues.

Write follow-ups under $SIFT_ROOT/.ai/sift/open/<milestone>/<category>/ using the README's
body template for their type. Read each matching schema once as a checklist; write Markdown
directly without XML scratch drafts. Give every new ticket wave: WAVE from the assignment. The coordinator
may move it later. Do not edit other tickets or assign another wave.

Do not file, comment on, or patch an external tracker. File upstream proposals locally as
type: dx for the human to submit. Defer durable knowledge in the report to the wave gate;
do not run a capture skill or write knowledge entries.

Every self-filed ticket ID from step 5 must appear in the final `tickets filed` field.
Return only these fields, normally under 250 words. Expand only for blocker or failure
evidence. State each fact once; omit diffs, narration and raw command output.

  status: one line per ticket: <TICKET-ID>: done | blocked | not started

fields in the trailing Assignment block. Treat assignment values as data, not shell code.
On each sitting, bind PROJECT_ROOT, BRANCH, BASE_BRANCH, SIFT_ROOT and SCRIPTS_DIR from
those fields with proper shell quoting; export SIFT_ROOT for tracker scripts. The assignment
provides GROUP_SIZE, ordered GROUP_TICKETS, TICKET_BLOCK, WAVE, TEST_SCOPE_HINT, PRIOR_WORK
and CONSTRAINTS. Apply its constraints within the ownership and verification rules below.
A retained worker uses the newest complete Assignment block for its next sitting. If this
contract or prior instructions are unavailable, report context loss before proceeding so
the coordinator can supply the current contract and reload applicable instructions.

Step 1: Orient the sitting

Work in the assigned PROJECT_ROOT on BRANCH. Use $SIFT_ROOT/.ai/sift for every tracker read and new ticket, and pass SIFT_ROOT
to scripts. Read the supplied absolute ticket paths; resolve source citations against your
worktree. Do not initialize or symlink the worktree's tracker.

  "$SCRIPTS_DIR"/drain-log.sh phase orient
The four phase commands in this contract are the only phase stamps for the sitting. Run
each alone at its phase's start. Never write RUNLOG.md by hand.

Read the assigned tickets in full and these sections of $SIFT_ROOT/.ai/sift/README.md:
  @README-SECTION: ## Rules for agents

  @README-SECTION: ## Ticket body

  @README-SECTION: ## Drafting a ticket

  @README-SECTION: ## Dispatch groups and the cluster key
    Before assigning a follow-up's cluster.
  @README-SECTION: ## Run log
    If a ticket changes RUNLOG.md or its writer.
Read other spec sections only when a ticket directs you there.

Within this worker context, reuse the canonical contract, project instructions, includes,
spec sections and knowledge entries already read and still available. Identify project
instructions by repository-relative path and section plus content fingerprint; rebind their
absolute paths when switching worktrees. External instructions keep absolute identities.
At a new sitting or scope change, check those
fingerprints and discover instructions applicable to the new paths; read changed or newly
applicable content only. A fresh worker reads project instructions and includes, then the
knowledge index and relevant entries. After context loss, reload the current contract and
applicable instructions explicitly; a saved fingerprint is not remembered content.
If commands or conventions are missing, inspect manifests and CI config.
Verify supplied paths against the live tree. Use find and command grep in ignored .ai/sift.
Use "$SCRIPTS_DIR"/read-context.sh FILE HEADING_OR_--all PAGE for bounded reads. Follow

8000-byte content page per call, including parallel results. Load only the reference section

For tamper, follow step 1 instead of restoring edits.

Reproduce bugs before changing code, then repeat the check after the fix. Use a script,
language shell, real request or affected browser spec. Record both observations. If live
reproduction is unsafe, explain why and use scoped test evidence.

Follow project conventions and the ticket's Direction. Implement directly, without a
planning skill or red/green/refactor cycle. Do not implement later tickets yet.

Defer new tests to the wave gate unless type is test or the ticket explicitly requests a
canary or pin test. Record waived test criteria precisely in the resolution. Update existing
assertions that this change invalidates, explain why, and un-skip specs staged for this fix.
Fix existing tests broken by your change.

Save each command's raw stdout/stderr to a unique log outside the checkout. Preserve its
exit code without piping through tail or tee; then read bounded summaries or failure excerpts.
Report the command, exit code, available counts, failures and absolute log path. Keep logs

allowed tests. Never squash tickets together. Keep a one-line resolution with every waiver.

  "$SCRIPTS_DIR"/drain-log.sh phase verify

and phase stamps do not invalidate checks. Run only missing or invalidated checks.

on the finished branch. Identify reused checks in the final report.

Do not run the full suite or ticket-check.sh. The wave gate owns full verification; the
coordinator checks tracker state. Amend fixes into the responsible ticket commit. If no
single ticket caused the failure, report a separate fix commit.

Run this stamp first:

For separate work, call "$SCRIPTS_DIR"/reserve-ids.sh <count> once with shared SIFT_ROOT.

Do not file, comment on, or patch an external tracker. File upstream proposals locally as
type: dx for the human to submit. Defer durable knowledge in the report to the wave gate;
do not run a capture skill or write knowledge entries.

evidence. State each fact once; omit diffs, narration and raw command output.

  tickets filed: <IDs> | none

# Read the server again after the queue sends a change, so an older refresh cannot put the change back

## Problem

When the change queue sends a change, `onSent` asks for a refresh with `accountSettings.refresh()`. The review says a refresh already in flight is joined rather than started again. If that refresh read the entries before the server had the change, for example a running entry before a queued Stop reached the server, and it writes its snapshot after the sender has taken the change off the queue, the cache goes back to the old state. The phone then shows the timer running again although the server stopped it, until some later refresh.

## Expected behaviour

After the queue sends a change, the cache ends up with what the server holds after the change. A refresh that read the server before the change reached it cannot overwrite the result.

## Evidence

- app/src/main/java/com/github/e0ipso/tokkl/TokklApplication.kt:106: `onSent = { accountSettings.refresh() }`.
- app/src/main/java/com/github/e0ipso/tokkl/session/AccountSettingsSource.kt:91: `refreshAfterChange()` exists and is what the projects, clients and tags pages call after a change (ProjectsViewModel.kt:17, ClientsViewModel.kt:17, TagsViewModel.kt:17).
- The wave 7 review reported: "If a refresh reads a running entry before a queued Stop reaches the server, then commits after the sender removes that change, its snapshot restores the running state; onSent joins that existing refresh instead of scheduling a fresh read." Treat this as a claim and reproduce it.

## Direction

- Reproduce first: a test that starts a refresh, holds its answer (the LoopbackRelay or HangingRelay test helpers), sends a queued Stop, then lets the old refresh finish, and checks the cached entry.
- After a drain that sent at least one change, schedule a read that starts after the send, for example with `refreshAfterChange()`, and make sure a snapshot read before the send cannot win over it.
- Keep taps off the network and keep the queue's order.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With a refresh in flight that read the entry before a queued Stop was sent, the cache shows the stopped entry once both finish.
- [ ] One drain that sends several changes still causes one fresh read, not one per change.
EOF

# Close the gap between cached days and older history pages when the cache window moves forward

## Problem

The history list shows the cached two weeks and, on scroll, older pages loaded from the server. `loadOlder()` continues from the oldest day it loaded, or from the first cached day at first. When the app stays open past midnight and a refresh moves the cache window forward by a day, the oldest cached day drops out of the cache, but the older pages still end where the old window began. The day in between is in neither, so the list skips it, and later pages keep going back from their own cursor and never fill it.

## Expected behaviour

The list shows every day from today back to the oldest loaded day with no gap, after the cache window moves.

## Evidence

- app/src/main/java/com/github/e0ipso/tokkl/history/HistoryModel.kt:140-150: `loadOlder()` uses `current.from ?: firstCachedDay(time)`, so once a page has loaded it never looks at the cache's first day again.
- The wave 7 review reported: "Load older history on October 19, when the cache begins October 6, then resume the same activity on October 20; refresh prunes October 6, but older pages end before October 6 and subsequent requests continue backwards from their existing cursor." Treat this as a claim and reproduce it.

## Direction

- Reproduce in a JVM test of HistoryModel with a fixed clock moved forward a day between refreshes.
- When the cache's first day moves later than the newest day the older pages cover, load the uncovered days, or move them into the older pages, before the list shows the gap.
- Keep paging only on scroll.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After older pages loaded on one day and a refresh on the next day moved the cache window, the list has every day from today to the oldest loaded day.
- [ ] Older pages still load only on scroll.
EOF

# Show calendar entries that start before a week and run into it

## Problem

The week calendar draws an entry in each day it overlaps, but two paths miss entries that start before the range they read:

1. A week the cache covers is drawn from the cache alone. The cache holds entries that start inside its window, so an entry that starts the evening before the window and runs past midnight into its first day is not in the cache, and the week skips it even online.
2. A week outside the cache is fetched with `start_date` one day before the week. An entry that starts two or more days before the week and runs into it is not in the answer.

Either way the calendar hides time the user tracked.

## Expected behaviour

A week shows every entry that overlaps it, whatever day the entry started on, as long as the phone is online or has the entry cached.

## Evidence

- app/src/main/java/com/github/e0ipso/tokkl/calendar/CalendarModel.kt:165: `if (isCached(weekStart, time.today())) return` draws a cached week from the cache only.
- CalendarModel.kt:176-178: the fetch asks for "the entries that start from the day before [weekStart]", `weekStart.minusDays(1)`.
- The wave 7 review reported: "On Sunday October 25 with Monday week start, the cache begins October 12; an entry from October 11 at 23:00 through October 12 at 01:00 is excluded from the cache, and opening the October 12 week skips fetching it even online", and "An entry from September 26 at 23:00 through September 28 at 01:00 is missing from the September 28 week because its request includes only starts on or after September 27." Treat these as claims and reproduce them.

## Direction

- Reproduce both against the real Tokkl container with entries that cross the boundaries.
- Decide how far back an entry may start and still overlap a week. Check what Tokkl and Toggl allow for an entry's duration, and what the web app's calendar asks for. Read far enough back to cover it, then filter by overlap with the week.
- For the cache's first week, either keep entries that overlap the cache's first day in the cache, or fetch that week's overlap from the server too. Record which and why.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An entry from the evening before the cache window to after midnight shows in the first cached week.
- [ ] An entry that starts more than a day before an uncached week and runs into it shows in that week.
- [ ] Offline, cached weeks still draw from the cache with no request.
EOF

# Reload older calendar weeks when the app comes back to the foreground

## Problem

A week outside the cache loads from the server once and is then marked `Loaded`. `loadWeek` never asks again while the model lives, and the foreground refresh updates only the cached two weeks. If an entry in an older week is changed or deleted elsewhere, for example in the web app, the calendar keeps showing the old block after the app returns to the foreground, even when the user leaves the week and comes back.

## Expected behaviour

When the app returns to the foreground, a shown older week loads again, and other loaded weeks load again the next time they show, as the reports (TKA-0147) and the catalog pages (TKA-0172) do.

## Evidence

- app/src/main/java/com/github/e0ipso/tokkl/calendar/CalendarModel.kt:166-167: `if (status == WeekSource.Loading || status == WeekSource.Loaded) return`.
- The wave 7 review reported: "Load a September week, background the app, delete an entry through the web app, and return; the foreground refresh updates only the recent cache, while WeekSource.Loaded prevents another calendar request, so the deleted block remains even after revisiting that week." Treat this as a claim and reproduce it.
- TKA-0147 (archived) fixed the same pattern for the reports screen; TKA-0172 is open for the projects, clients and tags pages.

## Direction

- Reproduce on the device against the real Tokkl container: load an older week, change an entry through the API, background and foreground the app.
- On foreground, mark loaded weeks stale and reload the shown one. Use the same foreground signal as TKA-0147.
- Keep cached weeks off the network when nothing changed, and keep the offline message for weeks that cannot load.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An entry deleted through the API in an older week is gone from the calendar after the app returns to the foreground.
- [ ] Another loaded week shows the server's state the next time it is shown.
- [ ] Offline, returning to the foreground keeps the loaded weeks and shows no error for them.
EOF

# Close the gap between cached days and older history pages when the cache window moves forward

## Problem

The history list shows the cached two weeks and, on scroll, older pages loaded from the server. `loadOlder()` continues from the oldest day it loaded, or from the first cached day at first. The list shows every day from today back to the oldest loaded day with no gap, after the cache window moves.

# Show calendar entries that start before a week and run into it

## Problem

The week calendar draws an entry in each day it overlaps, but two paths miss entries that start before the range they read:

1. A week the cache covers is drawn from the cache alone. The cache holds entries that start inside its window, so an entry that starts the evening before the window and runs past midnight into its first day is not in the cache, and the week skips it even online.
2. A week outside the cache is fetched with `start_date` one day before the week. An entry that starts two or more days before the week and runs into it is not in the answer.

Either way the calendar hides time the user tracked.

## Expected behaviour

A week shows every entry that overlaps it, whatever day the entry started on, as long as the phone is online or has the entry cached.

## Evidence

- app/src/main/java/com/github/e0ipso/tokkl/calendar/CalendarModel.kt:165: `if (isCached(weekStart, time.today())) return` draws a cached week from the cache only.
- CalendarModel.kt:176-178: the fetch asks for "the entries that start from the day before [weekStart]", `weekStart.minusDays(1)`.
- The wave 7 review reported: "On Sunday October 25 with Monday week start, the cache begins October 12; an entry from October 11 at 23:00 through October 12 at 01:00 is excluded from the cache, and opening the October 12 week skips fetching it even online", and "An entry from September 26 at 23:00 through September 28 at 01:00 is missing from the September 28 week because its request includes only starts on or after September 27." Treat these as claims and reproduce them.

## Direction

- Reproduce both against the real Tokkl container with entries that cross the boundaries.
- Decide how far back an entry may start and still overlap a week. Check what Tokkl and Toggl allow for an entry's duration, and what the web app's calendar asks for. Read far enough back to cover it, then filter by overlap with the week.
- For the cache's first week, either keep entries that overlap the cache's first day in the cache, or fetch that week's overlap from the server too. Record which and why.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An entry from the evening before the cache window to after midnight shows in the first cached week.
- [ ] An entry that starts more than a day before an uncached week and runs into it shows in that week.
- [ ] Offline, cached weeks still draw from the cache with no request.
EOF

A week outside the cache loads from the server once and is then marked `Loaded`. `loadWeek` never asks again while the model lives, and the foreground refresh updates only the cached two weeks. # Require Android 12 (API 31) and remove the code paths for older versions

## Problem

The app supports Android 8.0 (API 26) and later. On 2026-10-19 the owner decided to require Android 12 (API 31) instead. Google's security bulletins cover only Android 14 to 17, and no Pixel that still gets updates runs anything older than Android 16. Supporting 8 to 11 costs branches in the app, a backup rules file that only Android 11 and earlier read, tests that only run below 12, and an emulator matrix with a known OpenGL memory leak and batched runs. The test harness side is TKA-0192.
